s1.syndrome_frame: inflammatory arthritis and skin lesions with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: weight loss without fever or sweats
key_facts: male patient in his 50s
dermal papules on trunk and extremities
preference for extensor surfaces of arms and legs
no lymphadenopathy
normal complete blood cell count and metabolic panel
normal viral and rheumatologic panels
normal serum and urine protein electrophoresis
mild restrictive lung disease on pulmonary function tests
skin biopsy showed nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate
atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes on skin biopsy
low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal on immunostaining
clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements in skin and bone marrow
atypical lymphocytes in bone marrow with CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements and atypical lymphocytes on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy showing nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: atypical lymphocytes with inverted CD8:CD4 ratio on immunostaining

raw.rationale: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules with preference for extensor surfaces, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy, atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, and clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements in skin and bone marrow are characteristic of mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, mycosis fungoides is a specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Typically involves muscle weakness and characteristic skin findings such as Gottron's papules, which are not mentioned

rejected.label: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Similar to dermatomyositis but without muscle weakness, still does not fit the described skin and lymph node findings

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Involves erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and atypical lymphocytes in the blood, which are not present in this case
